title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Termly Exam #12 (Term 3)

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #12 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A pump pushing air into a tyre is an example of (1 mark)
   A. A force
   B. A shadow
   C. A colour
   D. A gas

2. Which of these can change the shape of dough? (1 mark)
   A. Looking at it
   B. Pressing with a force
   C. Leaving it alone
   D. Talking to it

3. Why do we put oil on machine parts? (1 mark)
   A. To increase friction
   B. To make them weak
   C. To reduce friction
   D. To make them heavy

4. Which of these holds a shirt together? (1 mark)
   A. Thread stitches
   B. A rolling wheel
   C. Oil
   D. Wind

5. Which force slows down or stops a book sliding on the floor? (1 mark)
   A. Friction
   B. Light
   C. Heat
   D. Gravity

6. Which of these shows that friction produces heat? (1 mark)
   A. Pouring water
   B. Rubbing hands together
   C. Drawing with chalk
   D. Looking at a torch

7. Where are ball bearings found? (1 mark)
   A. In bicycle wheels
   B. In a cup
   C. In a pencil
   D. In a book

8. Why does a mango fall from a tree? (1 mark)
   A. Friction pushes it
   B. Sound moves it
   C. Light pulls it
   D. Gravity pulls it down

9. Which of these is a way of increasing useful friction? (1 mark)
   A. Oiling a floor
   B. Polishing a table
   C. Wearing smooth socks on a wet floor
   D. Shoes with rough soles

10. What is a source of light? (1 mark)
   A. Something that is dark
   B. Something that reflects light
   C. Something that gives out its own light
   D. Something that blocks light

11. Why do houses have windows? (1 mark)
   A. To let in only rain
   B. To keep out light
   C. To make noise
   D. To let in daylight

12. A flash of light in the sky during a storm is a natural source of light. What is it? (1 mark)
   A. A car headlight
   B. A lantern
   C. Lightning
   D. A solar lamp

13. Which of these is a benefit of good lighting when reading? (1 mark)
   A. It prevents tired eyes
   B. It makes pages smell
   C. It makes books heavier
   D. It makes letters disappear

14. Which of these can be a cheap way of lighting a house in a rural area? (1 mark)
   A. A big generator
   B. Solar lamp
   C. Many electric heaters
   D. Hundreds of candles

15. Why are pot handles often made of wood or plastic? (1 mark)
   A. They pass heat quickly
   B. They pass heat slowly
   C. They get very hot
   D. They are heavy

16. In which unit is temperature measured in science? (1 mark)
   A. Degrees Celsius
   B. Metres
   C. Kilograms
   D. Litres

17. Which of these is a source of heat from burning? (1 mark)
   A. A cup
   B. A ruler
   C. A book
   D. Charcoal

18. Why does an ice cube melt in your hand? (1 mark)
   A. Heat goes from your hand into the ice
   B. The hand makes water
   C. Cold goes into your hand
   D. The ice makes heat

19. Which use of heat makes cloth smooth? (1 mark)
   A. Making shadows
   B. Playing music
   C. Reading a book
   D. Ironing clothes

20. Which of these uses heat to change dough into bread? (1 mark)
   A. Cutting
   B. Baking
   C. Washing
   D. Freezing

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain the difference between heat and temperature. (4 marks)

22. Explain how farmers use light to discourage pests and animals. (4 marks)

23. Name four safety measures to observe in a kitchen and give a reason for each. (4 marks)

24. Give three examples of things that use electricity to make heat. (3 marks)

25. Give three safety rules when using sources of light. (3 marks)

26. Describe how you would show that light travels in a straight line. (3 marks)

27. Explain how gravity helps and how it can cause problems in daily life. (5 marks)

28. State two ways of reducing friction. (2 marks)

29. Give two safety rules when using an electric iron. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #12 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — A force
   The pump pushes air by force.

2. B — Pressing with a force
   A force can squeeze and stretch dough.

3. C — To reduce friction
   Oil makes surfaces slide easily.

4. A — Thread stitches
   Stitches hold cloth pieces together.

5. A — Friction
   Friction opposes the movement between surfaces.

6. B — Rubbing hands together
   Rubbing surfaces produces heat.

7. A — In bicycle wheels
   Bicycle wheels use ball bearings.

8. D — Gravity pulls it down
   Gravity acts on every object.

9. D — Shoes with rough soles
   Rough soles grip the ground.

10. C — Something that gives out its own light
   A source of light makes its own light.

11. D — To let in daylight
   Windows allow sunlight to enter the room.

12. C — Lightning
   Lightning is a natural flash of light.

13. A — It prevents tired eyes
   Enough light makes reading easier.

14. B — Solar lamp
   Solar lamps use free energy from the sun.

15. B — They pass heat slowly
   Handles stay cooler.

16. A — Degrees Celsius
   Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius.

17. D — Charcoal
   Charcoal gives out heat when it burns.

18. A — Heat goes from your hand into the ice
   Heat moves from the warm hand to the ice.

19. D — Ironing clothes
   A hot iron flattens cloth.

20. B — Baking
   Baking uses heat.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Heat is energy that makes things hot. Temperature is how hot something is and it is measured with a thermometer in degrees Celsius.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for heat and 2 marks for temperature.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: They use bright or flashing lights at night near fields or animal pens to scare wild animals away. Lamps near sheds help to see thieves or pests.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for bright lights, 1 mark for scaring away animals and 2 marks for examples.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: Handles inwards to avoid knocking pots, gloves to avoid burns, children away to avoid accidents, switch off iron to avoid fire.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each with reason.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: Electric kettle, iron, cooker, heater, hair dryer, toaster.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Never look directly at the sun, do not shine torches in eyes, keep candles and lamps away from curtains and paper, do not touch hot bulbs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use three cards with holes in the middle and line them up in a row. Shine a torch through the holes. Light passes. Move the middle card and the light is blocked.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for set up, 1 mark for observation and 1 mark for conclusion.

27. (5 marks)
   Answer: It keeps us on the ground, makes rain fall and water flow downhill. It can make objects fall and cause injuries and break things.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for help and 2 marks for problems and 1 mark for a clear explanation.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: Smoothen surfaces, use oil or grease, use rollers, use ball bearings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: Do not touch it while hot, switch off after use, keep it away from children, do not touch with wet hands.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.
